guarantees.claim: All selector outputs (state_sel_o, add_rk_sel_o, key_full_sel_o, key_dec_sel_o, key_words_sel_o, round_key_sel_o) are initially driven to all-zero, and mr_err is driven to 0.

For each selector type (state_sel, add_rk_sel, key_full_sel, key_dec_sel, key_words_sel, round_key_sel), after the first loop the output is the bitwise OR of all corresponding sparse inputs mr_{type}[i] for i=0..Sp2VWidth-1.
mr_err is asserted (1) if for any i and any selector type, the combined output does not exactly equal the corresponding sparse input mr_{type}[i]. Otherwise mr_err stays 0.

assumptions.claim: External logic must not use state_sel_o, add_rk_sel_o, key_full_sel_o, key_dec_sel_o, key_words_sel_o, or round_key_sel_o when mr_err is asserted, because these outputs may contain an inconsistent OR of conflicting sparse selectors.
assumptions.risk: Using invalid selector values can cause incorrect cipher state progression or key expansion, potentially leading to secret exposure or loss of integrity.

uncertain_points.claim: When mr_err is asserted due to mismatched sparse selectors, the selector outputs continue to drive the ORed (potentially multi-bit invalid) value, and no safe default is forced. Downstream logic that does not use mr_err in the same cycle may propagate the corrupted value.
uncertain_points.cond: mr_err == 1 and at least two mr_{type}[i] differ
uncertain_points.risk: Invalid selector encoding (e.g., multiple bits set) could reach state and key logic, causing cryptographic misoperation or leakage before the error is handled.

uncertain_points.claim: If any sparse input mr_*_sel[i] is unknown (X) due to reset or initialization, the OR may produce X on the outputs, and the equality check (X != X → false) can suppress mr_err, masking an actual inconsistency.
uncertain_points.risk: Transient inconsistency may go undetected during start-up, leading to a window where corrupted selectors are used without error indication.

uncertain_points.claim: If parameter Sp2VWidth is 0, both loops are skipped, leaving all selector outputs at all-zero and mr_err at 0. It is unclear whether an all-zero value is a valid and safe selector encoding for all modes.
uncertain_points.risk: An unintended zero-width configuration could silently disable all sparse selector combination without error detection, potentially causing the AES datapath to use default zero encodings incorrectly.
